# The organisation’s clocks

Move the first event and interval of discovery, decision review, funding and delivery across a 28-day event stream. A pinned alternative replays its timings under the current event stream and review attention assumptions.

Same-day events run discovery → review → funding → delivery. Each stage copies the information available at that time; later evidence cannot revise earlier choices. Repeated delivery slots count actions, not value. Evidence age and whether it still matches need are separate outcomes.

Reviews consume a bounded attention budget even without new evidence. The stable-need scenario shows why more reviews need not change actions; a late change exposes the risk of exhausting attention early.

Inspired by [John Cutler’s Questions and Context](https://cutlefish.substack.com/p/tbm-2052-questions-and-context); this explicit four-stage timing mechanism is our interpretation.
